Also worth checking: does the confirm dialog ever get dismissed/cancelled by an accidental Escape or outside click that a user might not notice, reading as 'reset did nothing'? Needs a real repro from the user (which action sequence, which photo state) before chasing further — left open, not closed.

E6.source: [found by tooling, not user-reported, 2026-09-08] the docked Library filmstrip (#lib-overlay, left column in deskx) does not re-theme at all — toggleTheme()/body.light never changes its background/text/border colours, which stay on dark tokens regardless of theme.
E6.note: 2026-09-09: ROOT CAUSE FIXED. #lib-overlay keeps its OWN theme class (.lib-light) separate from body.light, only synced from its own boot/click handlers, never when the Editor's toggleTheme()/fxSetTheme() ran (they share the 'csTheme' localStorage KEY but were never wired to react to each other live). Added window.chromasmithSyncLibTheme (desktop/library-ui.js) called from both chromasmith-22.html theme functions, and made the Library's own opt.onclick set body.light in the reverse direction too — now genuinely two-way. Verified live in the Browser pane, both directions, both themes (confirmed via a hard cache-bust after an unrelated Browser-pane script-caching artifact briefly made the fix look broken). backgroundColor/color findings now clear. RESIDUAL, still open: a borderColor finding remains — the dock's border mixes light/dark per-side colours in light theme (a narrower, separate CSS gap from the theme-sync bug just fixed), left as a visible failing finding rather than allowlisted. 2026-09-09 (follow-up): border-colour residual re-checked live in the Browser pane (docked, light theme, .lib-light applied, tab active/inactive, photo loaded) across every bordered element in the filmstrip (#lib-overlay, #lib-side, .lib-side-tabs, both tab buttons, #lib-top, .lib-dock-resizer) via getComputedStyle per side — every visible (non-zero-width) border resolved to the same theme-correct hairline token, no mismatch found. User independently confirmed the docked filmstrip's border looks consistent in light theme on the real app. Marking FIXED (not reproducible); the only mismatches found were 0px-width sides falling back to currentColor, invisible and already noted as a known non-issue in the code's own comment (library-ui.js ~line 785).

E7.source: [found by tooling, not user-reported, 2026-09-08] intermittent (roughly half of runs observed): in light theme, once a photo is loaded, the topbar/undo-cluster/rail/tool-panel text colour reverts to the DARK-theme colour (white) even though body.light is set. Same inputs, different result across runs.
E7.note: Scoped into this pass per user 2026-09-08. RESOLVED 2026-09-10: root cause was NOT a CSS/theme bug — --txt/body.light were always correct. The real cause is chromasmithForceLibraryReady() (desktop/library-ui.js, boot watchdog) winning a timing race against the harness's own load/settle window and force-flipping the Library into full-view takeover (body.lib-full, hides #fx-deskbar) mid-run; whatever remained visible then read different computed styles across the board, with color being the property most often reported. Confirmed by 4x clean reruns of editor_wireframe_diff.mjs against an unmodified tree: 16 findings → 0 → 0 → 0. Mitigated by widening the watchdog's initial grace period 10000ms→16000ms (chromasmith-22.html, window.bumpBootSplashWatchdog) so real boot has more room before the safety valve fires, cutting the race window with the harness.

3.1.5.note: DIAGNOSED LIVE 2026-09-09, NOT a dead-control bug — the toggle, uniform plumbing, and shader branch are all correctly wired (confirmed: fxGamutWarn flips, .on class updates, render() receives gamutWarn). The shader's OWN comment (chromasmith-22.html ~6360, 'KNOWN SCOPE LIMIT') explains why nothing visibly changes for a normal edit: the 'lut' FBO is an 8-bit RGBA texture, so basicAdjust/curves/masks clipping (a big Exposure push, confirmed tested at slider=100 — canvas hash genuinely didn't change) is already hard-clamped by the GPU texture write BEFORE the gamut check ever runs. Only clipping introduced AFTER that point (grain's unclamped addition, print-LUT output) is currently catchable — not tested live yet. This makes the feature effectively invisible for the most common trigger (exposure/highlight recovery), which is very likely why the user experiences it as 'doesn't work' even though it isn't dead code. The code already names its own fix: force hdrIntermediate (RGBA16F) whenever the toggle is on, to extend coverage upstream of the 8-bit clamp. NOT implemented — real shader/perf tradeoff, needs a decision before touching it (see plan).

3.4.6.source: BUG: Highlight Response doesn't seem to do anything to the photo
3.4.6.note: DIAGNOSED LIVE 2026-09-09, same shape as 3.1.5 (not a dead-control bug): confirmed live that switching sel-tonemap to 'agx' produces zero canvas change with the test fixture (portrait.png, an 8-bit non-RAW PNG). Traced the shader (chromasmith-22.html useTonemap uniform, ~line 6266): the whole point of the AgX/BT.2390 rolloff is to preserve values ABOVE 1.0 (real highlight headroom) instead of hard-clamping — an 8-bit source with no values above 1.0 has nothing to roll off, so AgX/Standard/clamp all converge to the same output BY DESIGN. The control's own tooltip already says this ('Only visible once real RAW highlight headroom survives to the render'). Untested: whether it actually differs on a genuine blown-highlight RAW capture — that's the real thing to verify before concluding this is fully working, but the shader logic itself looks sound and matches its documentation. Likely a discoverability/UX problem (nothing tells the user why nothing happened on their photo), not dead code — separate from 3.4.7's 'should be moved' (a layout ask, independent of this).

E9.note: 2026-09-09: Root cause was #lib-top (the full Library toolbar) staying display:flex while docked (body.deskx #lib-overlay:not(.full) never hid it) — confirmed live via a real screenshot from the user, and reproduced/measured in the Browser pane (199px of chrome above the tabs at every dock width). Architecture changed per user request: instead of a growing per-element CSS selector allowlist (previously 9 separate selectors across two rules, one miss — #lib-top — being exactly this bug), every full-view-only element now carries a single shared class, .lib-fullview-only, at its own definition site (#lib-top/#lib-filters/#lib-viewbar/#lib-bottom/#lib-filters-panel/#lib-collections/#lib-folders-header/#lib-tree/#lib-collections-post), and the docked-mode CSS collapses to ONE rule: body.deskx #lib-overlay:not(.full) .lib-fullview-only{display:none}. T30.source: [audit of the testing tools, 2026-09-10, from the mskRebuild()/fxEnsureDepthMap() infinite-loop hang] the actual bug shape — a rebuild function chaining `somePromise().then(()=>rebuildSameThing())` with no attempt/memoization guard, where the promise's own failure condition is a STABLE condition the rebuild re-observes on every call — is a generic footgun, not specific to Depth Range, and nothing in the testing tools looks for this pattern anywhere else in chromasmith-22.html
T30.note: Same class of two-things-drift risk as T2/T27 but for a CONTROL-FLOW shape instead of a data list: a function that calls itself again (directly or by name) inside a `.then()` off its own return value, with no local guard variable checked before the call, will loop forever the instant that promise's resolution doesn't change the condition that triggered it — exactly what fxEnsureDepthMap()/mskRebuild() did. Built a static source-text check (test/editor_self_reschedule_check.mjs) that flags `X(...)` calls inside `.then(()=>{...})` bodies where `X` matches the name of the function the `.then()` chain's own call sits inside AND no identifier containing 'attempt'/'running'/'pending' appears anywhere in that function's body — a heuristic, not a proof, but it would have flagged this exact function on sight.

T32.source: [testing-tool gap audit, 2026-09-11, researched against current WebGL testing practice] nothing measures GPU/texture memory across repeated LUT swaps, mask rebuilds, or tile-export runs — a slow leak (e.g. an uncleared WebGLBuffer/WebGLUniformLocation on every redraw, a documented WebGL failure pattern) would never show up in export_harness.mjs's one-shot renders.
T32.note: Needs a stress loop (hundreds of LUT swaps / mask rebuilds / tiled exports in one page session) sampling performance.memory or a WebGL context-loss/texture-count probe between iterations, asserting no monotonic growth.

T33.source: [testing-tool gap audit, 2026-09-11] resizing an on-screen WebGL canvas is a documented WebKit/iOS Safari memory-leak trigger (Apple Developer Forums thread 668999) — directly relevant since the shipping desktop/iOS engine IS WebKit — and nothing here resizes the FXR canvas repeatedly and checks for growth.
T33.note: A loop that resizes the preview canvas (window resize / panel open-close / loupe toggle, all of which resize the backing store) N times and checks performance.memory doesn't grow monotonically. CLOSED 2026-09-11: test/editor_canvas_resize_leak.mjs resizes the viewport (4 sizes, 15 cycles) with a forced GC before each JS-heap sample, comparing early-run vs late-run mean heap size (trend, not a single delta, to tolerate normal allocator noise). Wired as `npm run editor:canvas-resize-leak` and into editor:gates as advisory (heap-growth measurement is inherently noisier than a structural check). Verified live: 15 cycles, 1.7% growth, well under the 40% threshold. Chromium doesn't reproduce the WebKit-specific bug this was researched from, but does catch a genuine leak in the app's OWN resize handling; T34's webkit-smoke is the complementary engine-specific gate.

T34.source: [testing-tool gap audit, 2026-09-11] docs/testing.md already documents that every gate here drives Chromium via Playwright, never the real WKWebView engine the shipping desktop (Tauri) and iOS (Capacitor) apps render with — the single largest structural blind spot: a shader/CSS/JS bug specific to WebKit ships invisible to every gate.
T34.note: Playwright's webkit browser channel is the closest automatable approximation (still not the exact WKWebView build, but far closer than Chromium) — running export_harness.mjs/editor_wireframe_behaviour.mjs against it too would catch a real class of engine-specific regression current gates cannot see at all. CLOSED 2026-09-11: test/editor_webkit_smoke.mjs boots the real desktop/dist build under Playwright's webkit channel, loads a fixture, and confirms crossOriginIsolated + a real non-transparent WebGL render + zero console errors. Wired as `npm run editor:webkit-smoke` and into editor:gates (skips gracefully, exit 0, if webkit isn't installed locally rather than faking pass/fail). Verified live: passes clean against the current build.

T35.source: [testing-tool gap audit, 2026-09-11] coi-serviceworker.min.js is load-bearing for RAW decode (SharedArrayBuffer/COOP-COEP on GitHub Pages) but nothing verifies actual offline behaviour: cache-hit on repeat load, correct fallback on a stale cache, or a genuine offline reload after first visit — the standard failure signature ('repeat load as slow as first load') is exactly what's untested.
T35.note: A Playwright test that loads the page once, goes into `context.setOffline(true)`, reloads, and asserts the app still boots and crossOriginIsolated stays true — plus a load-timing comparison between first and second load to catch a service worker that isn't actually intercepting. CLOSED 2026-09-11: test/editor_offline_check.mjs verifies coi-serviceworker.min.js's register/self-reload cycle actually lands on crossOriginIsolated=true, then verifies the REAL offline claim (lutWarmCache() populates IndexedDB; a warmed preset resolves via presetBytes() with genuine network offline and zero errors). Found along the way that coi-serviceworker.min.js has NO Cache Storage layer at all (pure fetch-passthrough header rewriting) — a full page reload while offline fails with net::ERR_FAILED. That's a real, separate product-level finding, not a testing-tool gap, so it's tracked as new item T54 rather than silently fixed or hidden; this test logs it as a note without failing the gate on something outside coi-serviceworker's actual documented scope. Wired as `npm run editor:offline-check` and into editor:gates. Verified live: passes clean.

T36.source: [testing-tool gap audit, 2026-09-11] one behavioural test exercises undo/redo functionally; none hammer it (hundreds of edits, undo-to-start, redo-to-end) and check the history array doesn't grow unbounded or that memory is reclaimed after a long session.
T36.note: Needs a stress test: N slider edits -> N undos -> N redos, asserting final state matches, fxHistIdx/history-array length stays bounded, and no console error/hang. CLOSED 2026-09-11: test/editor_undo_stress.mjs pushes 30 slider edits (past the 20-entry cap), confirms fxHistory.length actually stays <=20, then undoes to the oldest SURVIVING entry (not the pre-edit start, which the cap correctly evicts) and redoes back to the last edit, asserting exact values both ways. Found and worked around a real timing subtlety along the way: fxHistoryPush's ~400ms debounce can take noticeably longer under main-thread/GPU load, so the test polls for the actual history-length change instead of a fixed sleep. Wired as `npm run editor:undo-stress` and into editor:gates. Verified live: passes clean.

T37.source: [testing-tool gap audit, 2026-09-11] loadSession()/_fxPristineDefault and the per-feature snapshot paths (masks, curves, HSL, wheels, point colors — CLAUDE.md's own lesson #11 on typed-array/snapshot pitfalls) are load-bearing but nothing round-trips a session with every feature touched, reloads it, and diffs restored state byte-for-byte against what was saved.

T54.source: [found while building T35's offline test, 2026-09-11] coi-serviceworker.min.js has no Cache Storage usage at all — its fetch handler is pure passthrough (fetch(request).then(rewrite headers)). A full page reload while genuinely offline fails outright (net::ERR_FAILED), even after a first successful visit. CLAUDE.md §2's 'genuinely offline-capable after one visit' claim is true only for LUT preset DATA (via lutWarmCache()->IndexedDB), not for the HTML/JS app shell surviving a cold reload with no network.
T54.note: This is a product-scope decision, not an obvious bug fix: either (a) accept 'stay on the page while offline, don't rely on reload' as the real guarantee and adjust the CLAUDE.md claim to be precise about what's cached (LUT data) vs not (the shell), or (b) extend the service worker with an actual Cache Storage app-shell strategy (cache chromasmith-22.html + its same-origin assets on install, serve from cache when the network fetch fails) — a bigger, deliberate change to a vendored third-party file that should be a conscious choice, not a side effect of a testing pass. Left open for the user to decide which.
